root_cause.text: The ext2_iget() function fails to reject inodes with i_nlink == 0, a non-zero i_mode, and zero i_dtime, allowing corrupted inodes with zero link count to be loaded into the VFS, which later triggers a WARN_ON in drop_nlink() when operations attempt to decrement an already-zero link count.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the validation condition from `if (inode->i_nlink == 0 && (inode->i_mode == 0 || ei->i_dtime))` to check all cases of `i_nlink == 0`, adding an else clause to report an error and return -EFSCORRUPTED when the inode has zero i_nlink but valid mode and no dtime. The CVE description explicitly states that "the case of i_nlink == 0 with a non-zero mode and zero dtime slips through" and that a crafted image can exploit this gap to trigger WARN_ON inside drop_nlink() via ext2_unlink(), ext2_rename(), and ext2_rmdir().
